pages.browseTools.clearVisitsBody_other: {count} entries. Once cleared, they won't appear in recently visited or as suggestions in the address bar, and they can't be restored. Site logins and cookies aren't affected (use "Clear browsing data" for those).

pages.browseTools.cookiesHintSite: You'll be signed out of this site and need to sign in again. Your ergo sign-in isn't affected

pages.inbox.hint: {name} won't bring up what lands here unprompted. Items holding up a task must be handled before they can be archived or deleted.
pages.inbox.botTag: ⚠ Looks like automated access from the internet. Deny it if it isn't your device
pages.inbox.deleteBody: They'll be removed from the Inbox and can't be restored (the cards themselves stay in the chat).
pages.inbox.deleteSkipped_one: {count} more is holding up a task and hasn't been handled, so it's skipped.
pages.inbox.deleteSkipped_other: {count} more are holding up tasks and haven't been handled, so they're skipped.
pages.pairing.note.denied: The last pairing request was denied.
pages.pairing.note.expired: The last pairing request expired (not approved within {duration}).
pages.pairing.note.revoked: This device's credential was revoked in ergo. To keep using ergo on this device, request pairing again.
pages.pairing.note.credentialExpired: This device's credential expired (unused for too long, or never used after it was issued). To keep using ergo on this device, request pairing again.
pages.pairing.nameInvalid: The device name can't be empty or too long
pages.pairing.nameEmpty: The device name can't be empty
pages.pairing.pairedHint: This device has its credential (kept only in the browser's HttpOnly cookie, valid for {duration}, renewed each time it's used).
pages.pairing.intro: This is ergo. This device isn't paired with ergo yet: tap "{label}", then check and approve the request on the PC itself or on a paired device, and this device is ready to go.
pages.pairing.nameLabelIntro: Device name (you can change it; it's what the approver sees)
pages.pairing.nameLabelWaiting: Device name (you can change it; the pending request updates to match)
pages.pairing.waitingHint: Open ergo on the PC itself or on a paired device: this device's pairing request will show up in the Inbox. Approve it once the device name, short code and short fingerprint match.
pages.pairing.approve.title: Approve new device
pages.pairing.approve.matchHint: The new device should show exactly the same:
pages.pairing.approve.expired: Expired: request again on the new device
pages.pairing.approve.warning: If anything doesn't match, deny it: someone may be posing as your device. Once approved, the device gets a long-term credential you can revoke at any time.

pages.projectNow.chatOnRight: Keep talking in the owner session on the right.
pages.projectNow.buildDone: The first version is done and needs your confirmation
pages.projectNow.noOperations: The operations plan has no services or scheduled tasks yet.
pages.projects.title: Projects
pages.projects.wallHint: New projects come from {name}'s project suggestion card (asking for a project or tapping "New project" also gets you this card from {name}), or from turning a task into a project.
pages.projects.newToast: {name} will send you a project suggestion card. Tap "Start project" and the project is created
pages.projects.new.title: New project
pages.projects.new.what: What project do you have in mind (something long-term)
pages.projects.new.placeholder: e.g. Keep the warranties, manuals and repair records for my home appliances in one place, and remind me before a warranty runs out
pages.projects.new.hint: {name} turns this into a project suggestion card (a name and a one-line goal). Tap "Start project" and the project starts in preparation: the owner goes through kickoff questions with you and then delivers the project charter.
pages.projects.workdir.external: External path {path} (not in ergo's backups; relies on the project's own git remote)
pages.projects.missing: No such project (it may have been deleted)
pages.projects.side.title: Project records
pages.projects.side.hideTitle: Hide project records (tap "Project records" in the title bar to reopen)
pages.projects.side.resize: Drag to resize the project records
pages.projects.readOnlyInRecords: This project is archived, so the owner chat is read-only. To keep talking, unarchive it in the project records first
pages.projects.deleteToast: Confirm deleting "{name}" once more in Inbox
pages.projects.kindPending: Project type set when the charter is confirmed
pages.projects.announceHint: : when the owner sends an update, {name} reads you the key points right away, without asking first, in the owner's own voice if it has one
pages.projects.announceOnToast: Spoken updates are on: updates are read to you without asking first
pages.projects.announceOffToast: Spoken updates are off: you'll be asked before an update is read
pages.projects.archivedNote: Archived: the owner chat is read-only. Deleting needs a second confirmation and removes the project records and the owner chat; what you said there is kept as material.
pages.projects.standard.title: Standard
pages.projects.standard.legacy: Created before the project standard; no version recorded
pages.projects.standard.kindPending: Project type not decided yet, so three documents for now; a development project adds an architecture diagram
pages.projects.standard.newer: {latest} is out: not applied automatically; the owner proposes it and you confirm
pages.projects.internalHint: Started and run by the owner inside the project, not on the global board
pages.projects.pipelineHint: One at a time, first come first served
pages.projects.toolkitReadOnly: The project is archived, so the toolkit can't be changed. Unarchive it first
pages.projects.toolkitPending: The toolkit comes with the confirmed charter (the owner proposes it in the charter; it takes effect when you confirm)
pages.projects.scopeHint: Reviewed when the session is compacted and after each work order
pages.projects.scopeEmpty: None. A scope review runs whenever the session is compacted and after each work order; overreach and scope changes you approved are recorded here.
pages.projects.internalEmpty: None. In "Talk to the owner", say "Follow a workflow: …" or "Start a task: …" (or type /workflow or /task), or tell {name} it's for this project, and it starts inside the project. When the owner thinks maintenance is due, it sends you a suggestion card.
pages.projects.noScheduled: No scheduled tasks. To add one, pick this project in "New task" and choose "On a schedule" under "When".
pages.projects.operationsEmpty: No operations plan in effect yet.
pages.projects.maintainerNote: The owner's understanding of the project lives in the project records, not in the chat. If it drifts, reset it (a new session rebuilds the understanding from the project records alone; the old session stays viewable): tap ⚙ in the owner chat's title bar and choose the option to clear the current chat. That's also where this project's own prompt and context usage are.
pages.projects.serviceHint: Whether the project's own services are online: see the entries under Now in the project records
pages.projects.scopeEmptyProto: None. A scope review runs whenever the session is compacted and after each work order; the results are recorded here.
pages.projects.readOnlyOnPage: This project is archived, so the owner chat is read-only. To keep talking, tap the title to open the project records and unarchive it there
pages.report.noPrototypeContent: The prototype has no content for this file
pages.report.title: Report
pages.report.noPrototypeFile: No real file in the prototype
pages.tasks.status.awaitingConfirm: To confirm · Plan needs your OK
pages.tasks.cancelTimed.title: Cancel this scheduled task?
pages.tasks.cancelTimed.body: Once cancelled, "{title}" won't run again and the task is cancelled too (it moves to Recently ended on the board); the chat and the record of each run are kept. To stop it for a while, use "Pause" instead.
pages.tasks.memoryCurator.title: Memory consolidation
pages.tasks.cancelJob.title: Cancel this scheduled task?
pages.tasks.cancelJob.body: Once cancelled, "{title}" won't run again and leaves the board; its run records are kept. To stop it for a while, use "Pause" instead.
pages.tasks.noPlan: No plan yet: {name} is working out what you want with you, then the owner doing the work drafts a plan.
pages.tasks.scopeEmpty: None. A scope review runs whenever the owner compacts the session (for project tasks: after each work order); overreach and scope changes you approved are recorded here.
pages.tasks.readOnlyDone: The task is done and no longer takes messages. To redo it, use "Redo…" in the "⋯" menu at the top right
pages.tasks.readOnlyEnded: The task has ended; the chat is read-only
pages.tasks.composer.timed: Change what each run does or add requirements; later runs follow the new version…
pages.tasks.composer.continue: Keep talking and it keeps working…
pages.tasks.composer.plain: Add details or change the requirements…
pages.tasks.toolkitEnded: The task has ended, so the toolkit can't be changed
pages.tasks.toolkitMulti: A task spanning several projects: this is what each project's owner is authorized to use on work orders (intersected with that project's toolkit). The task's own owner has a fixed toolkit (read project records, send work orders, sum up receipts) that doesn't follow this list, except for messaging {name}.
pages.tasks.toolkitProject: A task involving a project: at run time it can use the skills from both here and the project's toolkit. Abilities such as bash, network and MCP must be in both, so adding one here that the project toolkit lacks has no effect.
pages.tasks.noToolkit: No toolkit yet: it comes once the plan is confirmed (the owner proposes it in the plan; it takes effect when you confirm).
pages.tasks.runs.intro: Each trigger is one run. All runs continue the same chat, with a divider where each run starts (zoomed out, it's grouped by run). Triggers that arrive while a run is still going are batched for the next run.
pages.tasks.runs.workflow: Each run follows the authorized plan step by step, checking every step.
pages.tasks.runs.noneEvent: Hasn't run yet: it runs when the event comes.
pages.tasks.runs.noneTimed: Hasn't run yet: it runs when it's due.
pages.tasks.runs.batch: Triggered by this batch of {count} events:
pages.tasks.orders.intro: All of this task's work orders (including ones created but not sent yet). Work orders don't get their own cards on the board; receipts and project owners' questions are in the chat.
pages.tasks.usage.hint: Every model call is recorded. Usage for {scopeReview} and session {compaction} goes under the owner at the time, each on its own line, and counts toward the total. A rough cost estimate is under More · Usage.
pages.tasks.convert.title: Turn "{title}" into a project?
pages.tasks.convert.body: The project starts in preparation; this task's owner goes on with the kickoff questions (in the same chat) and then delivers the project charter. The task ends as "Done · turned into a project".
pages.tasks.convert.name: Project name (must differ from existing projects)
pages.tasks.convert.done: "{title}" became project "{name}": see the project list
pages.tasks.proto.noPlanCard: The prototype has no demo plan card for this task; its stages are below.
pages.tasks.proto.orders: All work orders this task sent. Work orders don't get their own cards on the board.
pages.tasks.readOnlyArchived: Archived task; the chat is read-only
pages.tasks.proto.noChat: The prototype has no demo chat for this task. Try these: {tasks}.
pages.toolkit.catalogFailed: Couldn't load the skill library and MCP registry: {reason}
pages.toolkit.changed: Toolkit updated. If the owner is working, it switches to the new toolkit after its current step
pages.toolkit.mcpOwn: {name}: made from this project, always here
pages.toolkit.bashHint: Git Bash only. Generic bash and typed bash tools are still checked by the guard
pages.toolkit.networkHint: When off, network tools and commands are refused (best effort, not hard isolation). When on, read-only GET requests don't bother you; other requests count as "sending out in my name"
pages.toolkit.liveHint: Changes here take effect immediately, no plan change needed. The owner can add or remove skills itself, but asks you first before turning on bash, adding MCP servers or going online.
pages.toolkit.protoChanged: Toolkit updated: after its current step, the agent restarts with the new toolkit
pages.toolkit.protoBashHint: Git Bash only. Generic bash is still checked by the guard
pages.toolkit.protoNetworkHint: When off, network tools and commands are refused (best effort, not hard isolation)
pages.toolkit.protoHint: Changes here take effect immediately, no plan change needed. When the owner needs more capabilities, it submits a "toolkit change" card.
pages.about.connection.unknown: Unknown (couldn't check whether this page is trusted)
pages.about.debugOpen_one: Debug tools are open ({count} minute left) ›
pages.about.debugOpen_other: Debug tools are open ({count} minutes left) ›
pages.about.noEntry: The changelog has no entry for {version} yet.
pages.appearance.deviceOnlySystemDark: This device only. Your system is currently dark
pages.appearance.deviceOnlySystemLight: This device only. Your system is currently light
pages.appearance.styleHint: Every style has a light and a dark version (preview: light on the left, dark on the right), following the choice above
pages.appearance.fontScale.label: Text size
pages.appearance.fontScale.hint.narrow: Saved on this device for phone width only. Unfolded, tablet and computer widths each keep their own size
pages.appearance.fontScale.hint.medium: Saved on this device for unfolded width only. Phone, tablet and computer widths each keep their own size
pages.appearance.fontScale.hint.wide: Saved on this device for tablet and computer width only. Phone and unfolded widths each keep their own size
pages.appearance.fontScale.previewBody: With bigger text, the title bar and navigation grow only a little, so messages keep the room.
pages.userName.title: My name
pages.userName.sub: This is your name (same on all devices), not your assistant's: agents call you by it when they talk to you and when they read something out. Leave it empty and they just call you "you"
pages.authorizedFolders.title: Folders agents can read without asking
pages.authorizedFolders.intro: Once authorized, every agent can read files in these folders without asking you. This also works in the phone app's built-in browser: {name} looks here first when finding photos and files, and when handing files to a web page's upload box. Only reading is opened up: writing, deleting and overwriting keep the usual rules. When you authorize a folder in a chat and confirm it on the card, it's added here too. These are folders on the computer {name} runs on, up to {max}.
pages.authorizedFolders.warning: What gets read is sent to your model provider. Don't authorize folders that hold keys or passwords.
pages.authorizedFolders.exceptions: {name}'s own data directory and program directory, and secret files such as .env and private keys, stay off limits even inside an authorized folder.
pages.authorizedFolders.full: Already {max} folders. Remove one before adding another
pages.folderGrants.title: Folder grants
pages.folderGrants.intro: Each agent has its own list: one for your personal assistant, one per project (used by the project owner) and one per task (used by the task owner); sub-agents and reviewers don't inherit them. In a registered folder, the kinds of access you ticked (read, write and delete are separate) no longer ask you; anything else works as before.
pages.folderGrants.howToAdd: Register folders in each agent's own ⚙. When a chat shows an approval card because it reached a folder outside its scope, you can also tap “Always allow”.
pages.folderGrants.never: Never allowed, registered or not: the config, secrets, database and program folders inside the data folder stay unwritable and the secrets area unreadable; secret files in a registered folder (.env, *.key, *.pem, secrets*, id_rsa*, credentials*) are refused for reading and writing.
pages.folderGrants.everyoneIntro: Authorized folders: every agent can read the files in them without asking. Only reading is allowed.
pages.folderGrants.none: No folders registered for any agent yet
pages.folderGrants.clearAgentTitle: Clear all of its folder grants?
pages.folderGrants.clearAgentBody_one: {count} grant. Once cleared, it goes back to the usual rules for these folders.
pages.folderGrants.clearAgentBody_other: {count} grants. Once cleared, it goes back to the usual rules for these folders.
pages.folderGrants.usesIntro: Every read, write and delete let through by a folder grant is logged. For bash, only the paths written in the command are logged, not every file the program actually touched.
pages.folderGrants.noUses: Nothing has been let through by a folder grant yet
pages.autoplay.title: Auto-play agents' voice replies
pages.autoplay.sub: This device only. New voice replies play automatically; older messages and ones resent after reconnecting don't.
pages.browsing.authorizedFoldersHint: Want to use files from your computer when uploading or filling in on web pages? Set it here (Settings · Data & devices)
pages.browsing.searchEngineHint: Used when what you type in the address bar of Browse in the phone app isn't a web address. This device only
pages.debug.appOnly: Only available in the phone app
pages.debug.copyFailed: Can't copy: the browser won't allow clipboard access
pages.debug.notOpenHint: Tap the version number 8 times in "About ergo" to open them. They stay open for 1 hour, or until you reload the page or reopen the app.
pages.debug.expired: Debug tools have expired: they'll be gone from Settings once you go back
pages.debug.permission.denied: Blocked (change it in the browser's site settings)
pages.debug.handedOff: {what}: handed off. See the notification log below for the result
pages.debug.sendingIn_one: {what}: sending in {count} second. You can switch to the background now
pages.debug.sendingIn_other: {what}: sending in {count} seconds. You can switch to the background now
pages.debug.localNotify.title: [Test] Local notification from Debug tools
pages.debug.localNotify.body: Sent at {time}. Tap to go back to Debug tools
pages.debug.fakeAlert.title: {name}: [Test] This is a fake message alert from Debug tools
pages.debug.fakeAlert.body: Not a real message; it isn't in the chat
pages.debug.chain.deviceClock: this device's clock (couldn't get the daemon's clock: {reason})
pages.debug.chain.set: Set for {time} (by {basis}). When it's due: a pinned Inbox item, a banner at the top and a system notification. Tapping it opens that Inbox item; delete it in Inbox when you're done.
pages.debug.notify.title: System notifications
pages.debug.notify.requestHint: "Request permission" shows the system prompt if it hasn't been asked yet (the system shows it only once per app). "Open system settings" opens the system's notification settings if it has been asked; otherwise it shows the prompt first.
pages.debug.notify.appTooOldNoNotify: App too old: it has no notification methods
pages.debug.local.title: Send one on this device only
pages.debug.local.appTooOldNoForce: App too old: it doesn't support this option
pages.debug.local.hint: The page hands the local one straight off (through the native bridge in the app, as a browser notification in a browser); tapping it brings you back here. The fake alert takes the same path as new messages from {name} (a banner at the top and a system notification); tapping it opens the chat, and no message is added there.
pages.debug.chain.title: Full pipeline
pages.debug.chain.hint: The daemon really goes through the reminder module: when it's due, it creates an Inbox item, pushes a notify event, shows a banner at the top and sends a system notification. The title starts with "[Test]".
pages.debug.records.title: Notification log (last 20)
pages.debug.records.empty: No notifications sent since the page was opened.
pages.debug.records.oldApp: Older app versions don't report send results: they're logged as "{label}". Check the notification logs in hilog.
pages.debug.clockDiff.tiny: Less than 0.1 s apart (within one round trip)
pages.debug.clockDiff.ahead: Daemon is {seconds} s ahead (within one round trip)
pages.debug.clockDiff.behind: Daemon is {seconds} s behind (within one round trip)
pages.debug.env.title: Version & environment
pages.debug.connection.outdated: Page is outdated (protocol version mismatch); reload it
pages.debug.connection.unpaired: This device's credentials are no longer valid
pages.debug.connection.title: Connection
pages.debug.connection.fromSnapshot: Started from this device's snapshot, fetched only what changed
pages.debug.connection.fromScratch: No usable snapshot on this device; fetched everything
pages.debug.connection.fakeUpdateToast: A new-version bar now shows at the top; Reload works as usual
pages.debug.connection.hint: Latency is the round trip of one read-only request over the WebSocket (the daemon's version). "Simulate a new version" just shows the bar once; nothing changes on the server.
pages.debug.log.title: Logs & local storage
pages.debug.log.empty: No console.error / console.warn or uncaught errors since the page opened.
pages.debug.storage.title: Local storage
pages.debug.storage.empty: Nothing from ergo in localStorage or sessionStorage.
pages.debug.storage.hint: The device credential lives in a cookie (the page can't read it); for sensitive entries such as credentials and drafts, only their presence is shown.
pages.debug.reset.title: Reset first-time prompts
pages.debug.reset.hint: The system itself shows the notification prompt only once: after a reset, "Request permission" usually won't show it again, so turn notifications on via "Open system settings". When the app is reopened, the page asks again as if it never had.
pages.debugVoice.title: Voice
pages.debugVoice.playback.label: Record {seconds} s and play back
pages.debugVoice.recognize.label: Record {seconds} s and recognize
pages.debugVoice.recognize.result: "{text}" · recognized in {ms} ms ({model}, {device}), round trip {total} ms
pages.debugVoice.recognize.onlyFiller: (this transcript was only the model's own filler phrases; discarded {chars} characters)
pages.debugVoice.recognize.strippedNote: (also removed {chars} characters of the model's own filler phrases)
pages.debugVoice.speak.label: Speak a test sentence
pages.debugVoice.speak.sentence: Hi, I'm {name}. This is a speech synthesis test from Debug tools.
pages.debugVoice.speak.result: Synthesized in {ms} ms ({model}, reference voice "{voice}"), round trip {total} ms
pages.debugVoice.hint: The app records natively; browsers record in the page. Recognition and synthesis go straight to the daemon's recognition process and synthesis service, not through a chat.
pages.devices.awaitingFirstUse: Waiting for first use (void if unused within {duration} of getting its credential)
pages.devices.awaitingFirstUseExtended: Waiting for first use · credential valid until {date} (extended)
pages.devices.lastUsed: Last used {time} · credential valid until {date} (renewed on each use)
pages.devices.lastUsedExtended: Last used {time} · credential valid until {date} (extended, renewed on each use)
pages.devices.expired: Credential expired after {duration} without use · last used {time}
pages.devices.neverUsedExtended: Never used even after being extended to {date}, so it's void
pages.devices.neverUsed: Never used within {duration} of getting its credential, so it's void
pages.devices.localTrusted: Connections from this computer's own port are trusted automatically; no pairing needed.
pages.devices.howToPair: How to pair a new device
pages.devices.howToPairText: In the ergo app on your phone, tap "Scan to connect" and scan the code under "Show pairing code" above; opening the same address in the phone's browser works too. The new device shows its name, a {codeDigits}-digit short code and a {fingerprintDigits}-character short fingerprint; approve it here once they match. Pending requests expire after {duration}.
pages.devices.previewPairing: Preview: the pairing page the new device sees
pages.materialDetail.missing: This material is gone (it may have been deleted)
pages.materialDetail.markedNoInfer: This material is now excluded from inference
pages.materialDetail.deleteNote: Same options as bulk delete: Forget removes it from the material store only, so it still shows in chat history; Delete completely also deletes the original conversation text; both also delete any image or file you saved with it; Don't infer keeps it but leaves it out of inference.
pages.materialDetail.deleteNoteIngested: This is outside info, so deleting it always deletes it completely: the material and its text in the chat record of the save are both removed, and can't be recovered; Don't infer keeps it but leaves it out of inference.
pages.materialDetail.noPageText: (no text was captured from this page)
pages.materials.keepingOnly: The memory plugin is off: no new materials are collected, but existing ones can still be viewed and deleted
pages.materials.searchPlaceholder: Search materials: every space-separated word must appear
pages.materials.badRange: The start must be before the end
pages.materials.noResults: No matches. Try other words, or search all time.
pages.materials.noneFiltered: No materials like that in this period
pages.materials.noneInRange: No materials in this period. Try going earlier
pages.materialsDelete.doneNoInfer_one: {count} material is now excluded from inference
pages.materialsDelete.doneNoInfer_other: {count} materials are now excluded from inference
pages.materialsDelete.intro: Materials are the raw input ergo uses to understand you: what you've said, how you reacted to outputs and approvals, and so on. You can also say "forget…" in a chat; {name} then shows you a memory deletion card to check.
pages.materialsDelete.listNote: Open one to see its content and source, or delete it on its own
pages.materialsDelete.voicesExtra_one: , plus {count} voice message with no transcript (deleted along with its recording)
pages.materialsDelete.voicesExtra_other: , plus {count} voice messages with no transcript (deleted along with their recordings)
pages.memory.materialsSub: Raw records {name} has collected from what you say and do
pages.memory.claimsSub: Conclusions {name} has drawn from the materials; open one to see its evidence chain and competing explanations
pages.memory.questionsSub: What's still unclear during consolidation, asked so it can be settled
pages.memory.filesSub: Me, family, important people, others: IDs, birthdays, phones and other facts you've confirmed
pages.memory.systemTagline: Works out what you really want from what you've said
pages.memory.systemSettingsSub: Experimental · a memory brief with each message, questions in passing, a weekly interview
pages.memory.experimentalNote: This memory system is still being polished: its behaviour and the data it stores may change. Everything stays on this computer. You can turn it off any time in Settings · Plugins (the data stays and comes back when you turn it on again); to delete something, use the bulk delete in Memory · Materials, or remove the plugin in Settings · Plugins with "delete its data along with it" ticked.
pages.memorySettings.brief: Bring related memories with each message
pages.memorySettings.briefSub: When what you say matches conclusions in memory, those conclusions and your original words are brought into the conversation with your message, so you don't have to explain the background (relevance is judged by local search, no extra model calls; nothing is repeated within one conversation). Turned off, memory is only consulted when needed
pages.memorySettings.briefLabel: Bring related memories with each message
pages.memorySettings.briefOn: On: related memories are brought into the conversation automatically
pages.memorySettings.briefOff: Off: no more automatic memory briefs
pages.memorySettings.wovenSub: When a related topic comes up, weave in one question naturally to understand you better (at most one a day, never when you're in a hurry; you can skip it or say not to ask; whether you answered is checked by the memory curator during the nightly consolidation). Turned off, nothing is asked and the questions stay in Memory · Question box
pages.memorySettings.on: On: a question may be added when a related topic comes up

pages.safety.title: Safety and budget
pages.safety.askFirstSub:
On: in chats, risky actions (like reading or writing files outside its workspace, sending things out, or running commands it can't break down) show an approval card first and only run after you approve; in tasks, anything the plan didn't authorize also asks you first.
Off: most of these just run and are recorded as usual (you can see them in the details); only the most sensitive ones (sending things out in your name, accounts and passwords, irreversible commits, deleting or changing files outside its workspace) still ask you. Takes effect right away.
pages.safety.askFirstOn: On: risky things ask you first
pages.safety.askFirstOff: Off: most risky things just run; the most sensitive ones still ask you
pages.safety.budget: Stop tasks that go over budget
pages.safety.budgetSub:
On: when a step of a task uses more than its budget, it first explains its progress, and at twice the budget it stops and waits for you; you can add budget and carry on. The owner only estimates how many calls a step takes, and the token budget is worked out from recent actual usage. Cached input counts as one tenth, and the Usage page numbers are not affected.
Off: usage is only recorded and nothing stops (when you pay with your own key, a task that goes off track keeps spending). Takes effect right away.
pages.safety.budgetOn: On: tasks stop when they go over budget
pages.safety.budgetOff: Off: tasks keep going over budget; usage is only recorded
pages.watch.intro: Before every tool call, the guard checks which categories it falls into and acts on their disposition. "{askFirst}" always asks you on the spot when it runs; only "{plannedOnly}" relies on approving the plan once. Changes take effect right away.
pages.watch.brokenTitle: The watch category settings file is broken
pages.watch.broken: {title}: the guard is blocking every tool call for now (check failed). Below are the last valid settings.
pages.watch.reload: I fixed it by hand, reload
pages.watch.brokenCopy: When repairing, the broken file is saved as {file} in the config folder.
pages.watch.builtinHint: Calls outside every category just run and are logged. Tools marked "{doThenTell}" (such as git commit) tell you when done. Chats have no plan, so "{plannedOnly}" works like "{askFirst}" there.
pages.watch.customHint: Custom categories only take exact rules (matching tools, paths, recipients, amounts). You choose the disposition, but when a call hits several categories the strictest wins, so you can't loosen the built-in categories or the two bottom lines. Categories judged by a model will come later.
pages.watch.deleteHint: Once deleted, it no longer matches. Running tasks that made it stricter when their plan was confirmed keep checking it as confirmed (you'll be told how many); the rest follow this page.

pages.startTask.hint.remindEvent: The reminder goes in the board's operating section and sends a notification each time the event happens. You can cancel it. To have an agent do something, choose "{option}".
pages.startTask.hint.remindTime: The reminder goes in the board's operating section; you can change or cancel it until it's due. To have an agent do something at that time, choose "{option}".
pages.startTask.hint.eventWorkflow: The owner lays out the steps (parameters can use the event's values), and you authorize them once on the plan card. After that it runs once per event, following the authorized steps and checking each one against the filled-in values, without asking you again. Events that arrive while a run is still going are batched for the next run; all runs continue the same session. It sits in the board's operating section, where you can pause, resume or cancel it.
pages.startTask.hint.eventWorkflowInProj: The owner lays out the steps (parameters can use the event's values), and you authorize them once on the plan card. After that it runs once per event, following the authorized steps and checking each one against the filled-in values, without asking you again. Events that arrive while a run is still going are batched for the next run; all runs continue the same session. It only shows inside the project (not on the task board); pause, resume or cancel it in the project records.
pages.startTask.hint.eventPlain: Once created it's registered and runs in the background when the event comes. Each event is one run, and the details of that batch of events (file paths, task IDs…) are handed to the agent. Events that arrive while a run is still going are batched for the next run; all runs continue the same session. It sits in the board's operating section, where you can pause, resume or cancel it.
pages.startTask.hint.eventPlainInProject: Once created it's registered and runs in the background when the event comes. Each event is one run, and the details of that batch of events (file paths, task IDs…) are handed to the agent. Events that arrive while a run is still going are batched for the next run; all runs continue the same session. It only shows inside the project (not on the task board); pause, resume or cancel it in the project records.
pages.startTask.hint.atWorkflow: The owner lays out the steps and you authorize them on the plan card. It runs the steps once at that time, then counts as done.
pages.startTask.hint.atPlain: Runs once in the background at that time and counts as done automatically. {name} passes the result on in the chat; keep talking in the task details and it carries on.
pages.startTask.hint.atPlainInProject: Runs once in the background at that time and counts as done automatically. {name} only says it's done; see the result inside the project, and keep talking in the project's chat to have it carry on.
pages.startTask.hint.scheduleWorkflow: The owner lays out the steps and you authorize them once on the plan card. After that it runs on schedule, following the authorized steps and checking each one, without asking you again. All runs continue the same session, so later runs know what earlier ones did. It sits in the board's operating section, where you can pause, resume or cancel it.
pages.startTask.hint.scheduleWorkflowInP: The owner lays out the steps and you authorize them once on the plan card. After that it runs on schedule, following the authorized steps and checking each one, without asking you again. All runs continue the same session, so later runs know what earlier ones did. It only shows inside the project (not on the task board); pause, resume or cancel it in the project records.
pages.startTask.hint.schedulePlain: Once created, the schedule is registered and it runs in the background on time (without clarifying with {name}). Each time is one run; a run that can't be done is marked failed, and 3 failures in a row pause it automatically. All runs continue the same session, so later runs know what earlier ones did. It sits in the board's operating section, where you can pause, resume or cancel it.
pages.startTask.hint.schedulePlainInProj: Once created, the schedule is registered and it runs in the background on time (without aligning with the owner or clarifying with {name}). Each time is one run; a run that can't be done is marked failed, and 3 failures in a row pause it automatically. All runs continue the same session, so later runs know what earlier ones did. It only shows inside the project (not on the task board); pause, resume or cancel it in the project records.
pages.startTask.hint.plain: Starts without clarifying with {name}: what you write is the task brief handed to the agent, and it starts as soon as there's a free slot. No planning, authorization or checks (protected areas and secrets are still blocked). It counts as done automatically, and {name} passes the result on in the chat; keep talking in the task details and it carries on.
pages.startTask.hint.plainInProject: Starts without aligning with the owner: the project's owner does it right in the project, also without clarifying with {name}. What you write is the task brief handed to the agent, and it starts as soon as there's a free slot. No planning, authorization or checks (protected areas and secrets are still blocked). It counts as done automatically, and {name} only says it's done; see the result inside the project. Keep talking in the project's chat and it carries on.
pages.startTask.hint.workflow: Once started, {name} first aligns with you on what you want and writes the task brief. Based on it, the owner lays out a series of steps, each with the conditions it must meet, reviewed and fixed up before going on the plan card. Nothing happens until you authorize it once on the plan card.
pages.startTask.hint.workflowInProject: Once started, the project's owner first aligns with you in the project session and writes the task brief. Based on it, the owner lays out a series of steps, each with the conditions it must meet, reviewed and fixed up before going on the plan card. Nothing happens until you authorize it once on the plan card.
pages.startTask.hint.longRunning: Once started, {name} first aligns with you on what you want and writes the task brief. Based on it, the owner drafts a plan in stages. Nothing happens until you confirm it on the plan card.
pages.startTask.hint.longRunningInProjec: Once started, the project's owner first aligns with you in the project session and writes the task brief, then drafts a plan in stages. Nothing happens until you confirm it on the plan card.

pages.dataSources.folder.title: Import folder
pages.dataSources.folder.intro: Put a vCard (.vcf) exported from Google Contacts into this folder. Ergo imports it and moves it to “Imported”. That's the only kind it recognizes for now; other files stay where they are.
pages.dataSources.folder.opened: Opened the import folder on the computer
pages.dataSources.folder.copyFailed: Couldn't copy — select the path and copy it by hand
pages.projectNow.goLive: Putting it in use — waiting for you to confirm
pages.projects.goLiveToast: Confirm on the card to put it in use: it's under “Now” and in your to-dos
pages.tasks.observedTitle: What the system found in the execution log for the latest submitted stage (not what the owner says); ⚠ marks files the owner's report mentions but the system didn't find
pages.personalFiles.via.confirmed: you confirmed it on a check card
pages.personalFiles.via.curator: suggested by the memory curator, confirmed by you
pages.personalFiles.quoteGone: (the original message has been completely deleted)
pages.personalFiles.intro: Fixed facts about you, your family and the people around you: ID numbers, birthdays, phones, addresses… kept word for word, latest first, older values kept as history. Everything here was confirmed by you; {name} never writes guesses in here.
pages.personalFiles.groupGuessed: Guessed from the relationship; you can change it
pages.personalFiles.linkedHint: This is the same as "My name" in Settings · Identity; changing it here changes it there
pages.personalFiles.anniversaryHint: You can add several, each with a name: wedding anniversary, the day you met…
pages.personalFiles.modeNote.forget: Gone from the file and {name} can't read it; the original words stay in chat history and the event log.
pages.personalFiles.modeNote.purge: Deleted completely, together with its history, check cards and records of {name} reading it; this can't be undone. Anything {name} repeated in replies can't be removed.
pages.personalFiles.withSourcesNote: The messages you said in chat (and their memory materials) are erased the same way as deleting materials.
pages.memory.dataSourcesSub: Data brought in from outside (camera, calendar, email, bills…): connect, sync, disconnect
pages.personalFiles.withSources_one: Also delete the original message completely (1)
pages.personalFiles.withSources_other: Also delete the original messages completely ({count})
pages.memory.interviewSub: Get-to-know interview: one topic at a time, about ten minutes, stop any time
pages.memory.interviewActive: Interview in progress: {topic} — tap to continue
pages.memorySettings.interviewSub: The memory curator invites you once a week from your to-dos (monthly once all five topics are covered); one topic, about ten minutes, and you can say maybe later. Turn it off to stop the invites — you can still tap "Start interview" in the memory curator's chat or type /interview
pages.memorySettings.interviewOn: On: the memory curator will invite you once a week
pages.memorySettings.interviewOff: Off: no more invites; start one yourself when you like
pages.personalFiles.annual.notGregorian: Not a calendar date: yearly reminders for lunar dates aren't supported yet
pages.personalFiles.annual.remindersOff: The reminders plugin is off, so yearly reminders can't be set
pages.personalFiles.annual.onButOff: The yearly reminder is on, but the reminders plugin is off; it will be set once the plugin is back
pages.personalFiles.learned.empty: {name} hasn't learned anything about this person from your chats yet.
pages.personalFiles.learned.hint: From unified memory: what {name} has gathered and inferred from your chats about this person. Read only; never written into the file automatically.
pages.dataSources.lastDevice: Last sent from the phone {when}: {added} new
pages.dataSources.usage.importDevice: Accepted when the ergo app on your phone sends it
pages.personalFiles.via.contacts: picked from your phone's contacts, confirmed by you
pages.personalFiles.via.vcard: From an imported address book, confirmed by you
pages.dataSources.usage.importManualTo: Imported when you put a file in the import folder; {destination}
pages.dataSources.card.folderSummary: Drop exported files here; ergo imports the ones it recognizes
pages.dataSources.detail.notFound: No such data source: {id}. Its plugin may have been removed.
pages.dataSources.data.none: This data source has no data to show here.
pages.dataSources.data.fromDevice: The ergo app on your phone delivers this data. It can't be checked from here, so there is no “Available now” tab.
pages.dataSources.data.storedEmptyOff: Nothing fetched yet: import is off. Turn it on under Settings to bring data in.
pages.dataSources.data.rawHint: Raw data ({title}) covers {days} days. See it by day under Raw data in Settings.
pages.dataSources.data.liveNote: This is a live check. Nothing is saved to ergo
pages.dataSources.confirm.itemBody_one: {stop}, and this account's keys are removed from this computer; other accounts aren't affected. What about the {n} record it already imported?
pages.dataSources.confirm.itemBody_other: {stop}, and this account's keys are removed from this computer; other accounts aren't affected. What about the {n} records it already imported?
pages.devices.qr.title: Pairing code
pages.devices.qr.waiting: Waiting for the phone to scan
pages.devices.qr.scanHint: In the ergo app on your phone, tap "Scan to connect" and scan this. The code only holds the address; you still approve the phone here
pages.devices.qr.state.unreachable: The service manager can't reach it, which may be a problem on its side only. Try scanning anyway
pages.devices.qr.tailnetNote: The phone must join the same tailnet first
pages.devices.qr.rejected: {count} more entries can't be used by a phone. See "Outside access" under Settings · Checkup
pages.devices.qr.none.title: Ergo can't be reached from outside right now, so a phone can't connect
pages.devices.qr.none.body: Ergo only listens on ports on this computer. Something has to connect it to the outside before a phone can reach it (local network connections aren't supported). Pick one of these:
pages.devices.qr.none.managerTitle: Set it up in the service manager
pages.devices.qr.none.managerBody: A public tunnel or a tailnet entry both work; point it at the external port. The code appears here by itself once it's open
pages.devices.qr.none.managerOnComputer: Open the service manager on the computer running ergo: {url}
pages.devices.qr.none.managerUnknown: The service manager runs on the computer with ergo; ergo svc status shows its address
pages.devices.qr.none.managerOld: This version of the service manager can't tell ergo about its entries yet. Upgrade it to list them here automatically
pages.devices.qr.manual.title: Use your own address
pages.devices.qr.manual.body: For a reverse proxy, frp or anything else the service manager doesn't know about. It must be an https address that opens from outside and goes to ergo's external port
pages.devices.qr.request.title: A phone wants to pair
pages.devices.qr.request.expired: The request from {name} expired. Tap "Request pairing" on the phone again
